questions.reason: The Crawl reference's extract_depth description states verbatim that "`basic` extraction costs 1 credit per 5 successful extractions, while `advanced` extraction costs 2 credits per 5 successful extractions", which is exactly option b. The per-10-pages pricing in option c belongs to `instructions` and the availability condition in option d belongs to `chunks_per_source`, so neither is defensible for extract_depth.

The Extract best practices state verbatim "Extract accepts up to 20 URLs in one request." and the summary repeats "Batch up to 20 URLs in each Extract request", supporting option a. The page's only mention of 5 is the 1-to-5 range for chunks_per_source, so no distractor is supportable.

The Rate Limits page's Flex Tier Capacity section scopes exactly to the stem's scenario — "On non-paying plans, search requests that set `max_age_hours` are served under a flex tier. While Tavily is under heavy load, these requests are refused with `434 Flex tier capacity exceeded`. Retry shortly, or omit `max_age_hours` to be served from cache." The 429/432/433 distractors are documented on the same page or reference for different conditions (rate limit exceeded, plan limit, PayGo limit).

The Search reference's include_domains_mode description ends "Setting it without `include_domains` returns a 400 error.", which answers the stem's scenario directly. Options b, c and d restate other true sentences from that same description but describe behaviour when include_domains is supplied, so none of them answers what happens when it is omitted.

The Map reference describes select_paths as "Regex patterns to select only URLs with specific path patterns (e.g., `/docs/.*`, `/api/v1.*`)." — path selection without domain restriction, exactly the stem's requirement. The same page confines select_domains to domains/subdomains, exclude_paths to exclusion, and max_depth to distance from the base URL.

The Search reference defines results[].score verbatim as "The relevance score of the search result." The three distractors map to other documented fields on the same page (usage.credits, response_time, published_date), so exactly one option is best.

The FAQ's "What APIs does Tavily offer?" entry lists "**Tavily Search API** - A search engine designed for AI agents, combining search and scraping capabilities.", matching option a. Options b and c are the Extract and Crawl lines from that same list, and option d is from the separate "What is Tavily?" entry about the product overall, so the stem's scoping to the endpoint list leaves one best answer.

The Headers & Authentication example request sends "Authorization: Bearer tvly-YOUR_API_KEY" verbatim, supporting option a. The page assigns X-Project-ID to project attribution and X-Session-Id/X-Human-Id to session and end-user identification, none of which carries the key.
